ideas.title: Zone-designator sign split: definer computes UTC-minus-local with backwards operand order, gold applies the natural sign test (Lang FastDatePrinter)
ideas.mechanism: Faithful re-instantiation of the only structure that beat both models (CHART-PIE-03, 0/8). In the Claude PIE-03 trajectory the model computed the sign flip correctly and then wrote 'drift's Javadoc describes the displacement from the unexploded point to the exploded point' and ranked the DEFINER first, because the definer's name/doc ('drift between p1 and p2') read as contradicting its code (p1 - p2) while the gold ('Shifts an area by a displacement', x + dx) was locally self-consistent. Here the definer computes `offset = instant - wall` (UTC - local, backwards relative to the universal zone-offset convention local - UTC and to its own doc wording 'offset between local wall-clock time and UTC'), and the gold applies `offset < 0 ? '-' : '+'`, the textbook-looking test. Both are one-line fixes; the model resolves the ambiguity by contract-reading and blames the method whose code looks backwards. Time-zone sign is the canonical real-world sign-convention confusion, so the refactor is believable.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f (/Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v1/screening/lang), clean checkout. FACADE: src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinter.java, nested class TimeZoneNumberRule, method appendTo(StringBuffer buffer, Calendar calendar) (currently: offset = ZONE_OFFSET + DST_OFFSET; if (offset < 0) append('-'), negate; hours/minutes digits). Replace body with `buffer.append(DateFormatUtils.zoneDesignator(calendar, mColon));`. HOP1 add public static String DateFormatUtils.zoneDesignator(Calendar calendar, boolean colon): `final long instant = calendar.getTimeInMillis(); final long wall = instant + calendar.get(Calendar.ZONE_OFFSET) + calendar.get(Calendar.DST_OFFSET); return DateUtils.wallClockOffset(instant, wall, colon);` javadoc 'Formats the RFC 822 zone designator (-0500, or -05:00 with a colon) of the calendar's zone at its current instant.' HOP2 (DEFINER, analogue of PlotUtilities.drift) add public static String DateUtils.wallClockOffset(long instant, long wall, boolean colon): javadoc 'Formats the offset between local wall-clock time and UTC. @param instant the instant in UTC milliseconds @param wall the same instant expressed in local wall-clock milliseconds'; body `final long offset = instant - wall; return DurationFormatUtils.formatOffset(offset, colon);`. HOP3 (scale, analogue of Plot.nudge) add public static String DurationFormatUtils.formatOffset(long offsetMillis, boolean colon): `final int minutes = (int) (offsetMillis / DateUtils.MILLIS_PER_MINUTE); return StringUtils.zoneDesignator(minutes, colon);`. HOP4 add public static String StringUtils.zoneDesignator(int offsetMinutes, boolean colon) (needs import org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtils): `final int magnitude = Math.abs(offsetMinutes); final int hours = magnitude / 60; final int mins = magnitude % 60; StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(6); sb.append(DateFormatUtils.designatorSign(offsetMinutes)); sb.append((char)(hours/10+'0')).append((char)(hours%10+'0')); if (colon) sb.append(':'); sb.append((char)(mins/10+'0')).append((char)(mins%10+'0')); return sb.toString();`. GOLD HOP5 add public static char DateFormatUtils.designatorSign(int offsetMinutes): javadoc 'Returns the sign of a zone designator for the given offset in minutes.'; BUG LINE `return offsetMinutes < 0 ? '-' : '+';` CORRECT LINE `return offsetMinutes > 0 ? '-' : '+';` (the chain's offset is UTC - local, so New York's +300 must print '-'). CONTROL arm: in the original appendTo swap the two literals ('+' for offset<0, '-' otherwise). TRIGGER: existing org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinterTest::testFormat (sets Locale.US and TimeZone America/New_York, cal1 = 2003-01-10 15:33:20; first failing assertion `fdf = getInstance("Z"); assertEquals("-0500", fdf.format(date1));` all later Z/ZZ assertions flip the same way, so no assertion distinguishes the two fix sites). FAILURE TEXT: org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[-]0500> but was:<[+]0500> at FastDatePrinterTest.testFormat. Deterministic (fixed dates, explicit default zone, DST offset for July also flips consistently: -0400 vs +0400).
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtils#designatorSign — by construction (the control's swapped-literal bug is the line that moved into hop 5), and contractually: hop 2 names its inputs precisely (instant = UTC ms, wall = local ms) so the value it emits is unambiguously UTC - local; the leaf is the one method whose comparison is inconsistent with the documented data it receives. Behaviourally the definer's operand order is an equally short fix (same ambiguity PIE-03 had).
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateUtils::wallClockOffset (definer of the backwards-looking offset) at rank 1; StringUtils::zoneDesignator or the facade FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule::appendTo at rank 2; gold at rank 2-4.
ideas.model_specificity: Model-agnostic: PIE-03 fooled GPT-5.6 5/5 and Claude 3/3 by the same contract-reading heuristic. Slightly less robust than PIE-03 because time-zone sign is a well-known pitfall and a model may recall that Java ZONE_OFFSET is local-minus-UTC and call the leaf inverted; weaker models are marginally more likely to just blame the facade.

ideas.title: Swapped arguments at the gold call site hidden by name-aligned locals, callee javadoc misleading, callee pinned correct by two other passing callers (Lang Conversion chain)
ideas.mechanism: Inverts the depth/definer prior. The wrong-looking quantity `shift` is DEFINED in the deepest hop (NumberUtils.overlay), whose code is correct but whose @param docs describe index/at the wrong way round, so a reader sees doc-vs-code contradiction there (PIE-03 lesson: blame the definer whose doc contradicts its code). The real fault is one hop up: ObjectUtils.combine names its bit-position parameter `index` and its loop counter `at`, so the call `overlay(total, words[at], index, at, width, field)` lines up name-for-name with overlay's signature and reads as obviously right, while it is semantically swapped. Claude reads one hop per grep and never checks other callers; it will see a correct-looking call in combine and a doc-contradicting formula in overlay and rank overlay first. GPT-5.6, which does repo-wide greps, may find the two other correct callers of overlay and recover.
ideas.construction: Base: installed patch /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/diagnostic-noncanonical-v3/new_bug_variants/Lang/bug-1/L20/CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01/variant.patch on Lang-1f. EDIT 1 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.java overlay(final long holder, final long word, final int index, final int at, final int width, final long field): body becomes the CORRECT `final int shift = index * width + at; return (holder & ~(field << shift)) | (word << shift);` but the javadoc is rewritten misleadingly: '@param index the position in the holder at which the run begins @param at the index of the value within its run' (doc says at*width+index; code does index*width+at). EDIT 2 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ObjectUtils.java: signature `public static long combine(final long[] words, final long initial, final int index, final int width, final long field)` javadoc '@param index the position in the result at which the first value is placed'; body `long total = initial; for (int at = 0; at < words.length; at++) { total = NumberUtils.overlay(total, words[at], index, at, width, field); } return total;` GOLD BUG LINE is that call; CORRECT LINE `total = NumberUtils.overlay(total, words[at], at, index, width, field);`. BitField.widen's call `ObjectUtils.combine(words, initial, at, width, field)` is unchanged (positional). EDIT 3 (contractual pin) src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/Conversion.java: in shortArrayToLong replace the three bits/mask/out lines with `out = NumberUtils.overlay(out, 0xffffL & src[i + srcPos], i, dstPos, 16, 0xffffL);` and in byteArrayToLong with `out = NumberUtils.overlay(out, 0xffL & src[i + srcPos], i, dstPos, 8, 0xffL);` (add import org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils). ConversionTest.testShortArrayToLong and testByteArrayToLong keep passing, proving overlay's formula correct with correctly ordered args; swapping overlay's formula would break them, so the only all-green fix is the combine call site. CONTROL arm: facade `shift = dstPos * 32 + i;`. TRIGGER org.apache.commons.lang3.ConversionTest::testLang1112, first assertion intArrayToLong(src,1,0L,8,1): shift = 8*32+0 = 256 -> Java masks to 0 -> word lands at bit 0. FAILURE TEXT: junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: expected:<64729929216> but was:<252851286> (identical signature to the existing pair; second assertion would give 0x12345678CDF1F0C1).
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.ObjectUtils#combine — the call passes the bit position where overlay's run index is expected and vice versa; overlay's formula is pinned correct by two independent passing callers (shortArrayToLong, byteArrayToLong), so no fix in overlay keeps the suite green; the one-line all-green fix is swapping the two arguments in combine.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils::overlay at rank 1 (deepest hop, defines `shift`, doc contradicts code); combine at rank 2.
ideas.model_specificity: Hits Claude's one-grep-per-hop, zero-verification style hardest (it never greps callers of the gold: 0/56 runs searched a gold name before entering the chain). GPT-5.6's repo-wide greps for `overlay(` would expose the two correct callers and likely lift its Acc@1 to ~0.55-0.65. Weaker Claude tiers may not even notice the swap and fall back on the deepest hop, giving a similar ~0.35.

ideas.title: Angle-normalisation sign split: definer counts turns from the upper window edge with ceil, gold subtracts them (Math MathUtils.normalizeAngle)
ideas.mechanism: Second independent instance of the definer/applier convention split, in a different domain and with a weaker failure signal (assertTrue, no expected/actual). The definer computes turns = ceil((upper - a)/TWO_PI) - 1, a mathematically exact but exotic-looking expression equal to MINUS the standard floor((a - lower)/TWO_PI); it is the number of turns to ADD. The gold performs the textbook-looking `a - TWO_PI * turns`. A model verifying numerically finds the sign wrong and must choose between 'rewrite the weird definer as the standard floor' and 'flip the applier'; the PIE-03 heuristic (blame the method whose code looks backwards) and the pull of the standard idiom both point at the definer.
ideas.construction: Project Math-1f (/Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v1/screening/math). FACADE src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/util/MathUtils.java normalizeAngle(double a, double center) (currently `return a - TWO_PI * FastMath.floor((a + FastMath.PI - center) / TWO_PI);`) -> `return MathArrays.wrapAround(a, center);`. HOP1 add public static double MathArrays.wrapAround(double a, double center): `final double upper = center + FastMath.PI; return Precision.turnsToUpper(a, upper);` javadoc 'Wraps an angle into the window of width 2 pi centred on center.' HOP2 (DEFINER) add public static double Precision.turnsToUpper(double a, double upper): javadoc 'Counts the whole turns separating a from the upper edge of its window and resolves the wrapped angle. @param upper the upper edge of the window'; body `final double turns = FastMath.ceil((upper - a) / MathUtils.TWO_PI) - 1; return FastMath.unwind(a, turns);` (exact: equals -floor((a-lower)/TWO_PI) for all a). HOP3 (scale) add public static double FastMath.unwind(double a, double turns): `final double correction = turns * MathUtils.TWO_PI; return MathArrays.removeTurns(a, correction);`. GOLD HOP4 add public static double MathArrays.removeTurns(double a, double correction): javadoc 'Removes the given whole-turn correction from an angle.'; BUG LINE `return a - correction;` CORRECT LINE `return a + correction;`. CONTROL arm: facade `return a + TWO_PI * FastMath.floor(...)`. TRIGGER existing org.apache.commons.math3.util.MathUtilsTest::testNormalizeAngle (nested loops a in [-15,15] step 0.1, b step 0.2). First failure at a = -15.0, b = -11.8: upper = -8.66, (upper - a)/TWO_PI = 1.0096, ceil = 2, turns = 1, buggy c = -15 - 6.283 = -21.28 < b - PI = -14.94 so `Assert.assertTrue((b - FastMath.PI) <= c)` (MathUtilsTest.java:138) fails. Cases with turns = 0 (b <= -11.86) pass first. FAILURE TEXT: java.lang.AssertionError (no message) at MathUtilsTest.testNormalizeAngle(MathUtilsTest.java:138). Deterministic. Run only the trigger (`defects4j test -t ...`); the full Math suite is slow.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.math3.util.MathArrays#removeTurns — by construction (control's flipped operator moved into the leaf) and because hop 2's `turns` is exactly the standard quantity's negation as documented ('turns separating a from the upper edge'), so the leaf is the one hop that mis-applies its documented input; the definer is the alternative one-line fix (rewrite as floor from the lower edge), which the models are expected to prefer.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.math3.util.Precision::turnsToUpper at rank 1 (exotic ceil-from-upper definition), then MathUtils::normalizeAngle; gold rank 2-3.
ideas.model_specificity: Model-agnostic in principle; slightly less potent than LEX-01 because a model that actually evaluates ceil((upper-a)/TWO_PI)-1 for one pair discovers it equals -k and may then call the leaf wrong. The missing expected/actual pushes both models to read rather than compute, which favours the trap.

ideas.title: Exclusive-end span as gold, inclusive guard in the throwing decoy that owns the exception message, constants and @throws doc (Lang Conversion, exception trigger)
ideas.mechanism: Stack-trace vocabulary in a decoy plus a self-consistent gold. The IllegalArgumentException, its message '(nInts-1)*32+dstPos is greather or equal to than 64', the @throws javadoc stating the contract, and the `>= Long.SIZE` comparison all live in ArrayUtils.gather, which is the top production frame of the trace. The gold BitField.span returns `count * width + at`, documented honestly as 'the position just past the highest bit covered', so its code matches its doc; it has already returned when the throw happens and is absent from the trace. A model that evaluates span (=64 for two words at 0) and reads the doc concludes the guard is off by one (`>=` should be `>`) and blames gather; it also sits on a side branch at depth 2 while the value chain continues four hops deeper, so neither the depth prior nor the trace points at it.
ideas.construction: Base: installed CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01 patch on Lang-1f. EDIT 1 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/Conversion.java intArrayToLong: delete the `if ((nInts - 1) * 32 + dstPos >= 64) throw ...` guard (keep the nInts==0 early return); keep `return ArrayUtils.gather(src, srcPos, dstInit, dstPos, nInts);`. EDIT 2 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ArrayUtils.java gather(array, startIndex, initial, at, count): add javadoc '@throws IllegalArgumentException if {@code (count-1)*32+at >= 64}' and body prefix `if (BitField.span(count, at, Integer.SIZE) >= Long.SIZE) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("(nInts-1)*32+dstPos is greather or equal to than 64"); }` before the arraycopy/compose. EDIT 3 GOLD add to src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/BitField.java `public static int span(final int count, final int at, final int width)`: javadoc 'Returns the position just past the highest bit covered by a run of {@code count} values of {@code width} bits whose first value is placed at {@code at}.'; BUG LINE `return count * width + at;` CORRECT LINE `return (count - 1) * width + at;` (the guard compares an inclusive last-bit index). EDIT 4 restore NumberUtils.overlay to the correct `index * width + at` so the value path is clean. CONTROL arm: facade guard `if (nInts * 32 + dstPos >= 64) throw`. TRIGGER existing org.apache.commons.lang3.ConversionTest::testIntArrayToLong: calls with nInts 0 and 1 pass (span 32 < 64); the 4th assertion `intArrayToLong(src, 0, 0L, 0, 2)` (ConversionTest.java:553) gives span 64 >= 64 and throws. FAILURE TEXT: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: (nInts-1)*32+dstPos is greather or equal to than 64 at org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.gather(ArrayUtils.java:NNN) at org.apache.commons.lang3.Conversion.intArrayToLong(Conversion.java:NNN) at org.apache.commons.lang3.ConversionTest.testIntArrayToLong(ConversionTest.java:553). Deterministic.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.BitField#span — by construction (the control's nInts-vs-nInts-1 error is the quantity that moved into span) and because the facade's public contract (@throws if (nInts-1)*32+dstPos >= 64, unchanged in Conversion's javadoc) fixes the guard's comparison as `>=` on an inclusive index, so the value fed to it must be the inclusive one; changing gather's `>=` to `>` is the competing one-line fix.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils::gather at rank 1 (throws, owns message, constants, comparison and @throws doc); Conversion::intArrayToLong rank 2; gold rank 2-4.
ideas.model_specificity: Both models start from the trace and read gather first; GPT-5.6's habit of grepping the failure message lands squarely on the decoy. Claude will read span in the same grep as gather's guard (one call) and may notice the doc/contract mismatch with Conversion's @throws text, which is why its Acc@1 is estimated higher than for LEX-01.

ideas.title: Unit lie on the gold: `at` documented in bytes so the buggy `at * Byte.SIZE` is self-consistent; all upstream hops document bits (Lang Conversion)
ideas.mechanism: Javadoc that makes the gold's wrong code correct under its own contract, moving the visible inconsistency to the caller boundary. Every hop and the facade document the position in bits; only overlay says bytes and multiplies by Byte.SIZE. The model sees a unit mismatch at combine -> overlay and must decide which side owns the contract; because dstPos values 8 and 16 are whole bytes, converting at the caller is a viable fix, so the model may rank the caller (combine, or the facade) first. Weaker than LEX-01/02 because the whole API is bit-based and a model can argue overlay's contract is the odd one out.
ideas.construction: Base: installed CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01 patch on Lang-1f. Single-file edit src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.java overlay(holder, word, index, at, width, field): javadoc '@param at the offset of the run within the holder, in bytes'; BUG LINE `final int shift = index * width + at * Byte.SIZE;` CORRECT LINE `final int shift = index * width + at;`. Leave ObjectUtils.combine, BitField.widen, EnumUtils.compose, ArrayUtils.gather and Conversion.intArrayToLong docs saying 'position ... in bits'. CONTROL arm: facade `shift = i * 32 + dstPos * 8;`. TRIGGER ConversionTest::testLang1112: at = 8 -> shift 64 -> masked to 0. FAILURE TEXT: junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: expected:<64729929216> but was:<252851286> (second assertion, at = 16, shift 128 -> 0, would also fail).
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils#overlay — the facade's public contract and every upstream hop define the position in bits; overlay is the only method that reinterprets it, and its javadoc is simply wrong (a doc bug alongside a code bug). Converting at the caller would silently lose sub-byte positions, so the contract-preserving fix is in overlay.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.ObjectUtils::combine (immediate caller passing bits into a 'bytes' parameter) at rank 1, or Conversion::intArrayToLong; gold rank 1-2.
ideas.model_specificity: Roughly model-agnostic; Claude's evidence summaries in CONVERSION-LONG show it already tracks that `at` is dstPos in bits across hops, so it is somewhat likely to call overlay's byte doc the error. Weaker models are more susceptible to the self-consistent doc.

ideas.title: Static-import sibling swarm: same-name `overlay` overloads in BitField and NumberUtils, unqualified call resolved only by argument type (Lang Conversion)
ideas.mechanism: Search/candidate-overload trap aimed at the models' name-driven navigation. ObjectUtils.combine calls `overlay(total, words[i], i, at, width, field)` unqualified under two single-static-imports (BitField.overlay taking an int word, NumberUtils.overlay taking a long word); Java overload resolution binds to NumberUtils because words is long[]. Claude's `grep -rn "static long overlay"` shows two declarations in two classes; the BitField variant is an Msb0 implementation whose `Long.SIZE - width - (index*width + at)` shift looks wrong to a reader of an Lsb0 test, so a model that binds the call by eye picks the wrong class. Scoring is exact FQCN::method, so a wrong class with the right method name scores zero.
ideas.construction: Base: installed CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01 patch on Lang-1f (gold NumberUtils.overlay keeps its bug `(index + at) * width`). EDIT 1 add to src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/BitField.java `public static long overlay(final long holder, final int word, final int index, final int at, final int width, final long field)`: javadoc 'Overlays a value onto a holder using Msb0 bit ordering (the first value occupies the most significant field).'; body `final int shift = Long.SIZE - width - (index * width + at); return (holder & ~(field << shift)) | ((word & field) << shift);` (real, correct Msb0 behaviour; not executed by the trigger). EDIT 2 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ObjectUtils.java: replace `import org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils;` with `import static org.apache.commons.lang3.BitField.overlay;` and `import static org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils.overlay;` (legal: distinct signatures); call site `total = overlay(total, words[i], i, at, width, field);` (words is long[] so this binds to NumberUtils.overlay). Lang main code already uses import static (text/FormattableUtils.java). TRIGGER ConversionTest::testLang1112, FAILURE TEXT unchanged: expected:<64729929216> but was:<252851286>.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils#overlay — the overload actually bound and executed (long word), containing the moved control bug; BitField.overlay is never invoked by the trigger.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.BitField::overlay at rank 1 when the model mis-resolves the unqualified call (its Msb0 shift formula reads as the obvious culprit); otherwise gold rank 1 with BitField.overlay rank 2.
ideas.model_specificity: Claude-specific leaning: it greps declarations by name and reads the first -A window, rarely reads import blocks. GPT-5.6's broader greps and sed ranges usually include the import block, so it should resolve correctly most of the time (~0.75). Note the decoy is not executed by the trigger (the brief prefers executed decoys); neither model runs coverage, so this is unlikely to matter in practice but is a known weakness.

ideas.title: Gold as a private helper inside the nested FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule Rule class, chain returns the raw UTC-minus-local minutes (variant of LEX-01)
ideas.mechanism: Same sign-split as LEX-01 but the applier lives where real Lang code puts it: a private static helper in the nested Rule class, so the gold's FQCN is `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule`. Two effects: (a) the definer trap of LEX-01 still operates; (b) an exact-match scorer artifact: any submission spelling the class as FastDatePrinter.TimeZoneNumberRule or FastDatePrinter scores zero. Calibration from 47 past submissions naming nested classes (all HarmonicFitter$ParameterGuesser, all with `$`) says the misspelling risk is small (~0.1), so this is mostly LEX-01 with the gold moved into the facade's own class, which slightly HELPS the model (facade proximity) and partly cancels the artifact.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f as LEX-01. FACADE FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule.appendTo: `final int offset = DateFormatUtils.wallClockOffsetMinutes(calendar); buffer.append(designatorSign(offset)); final int magnitude = Math.abs(offset); final int hours = magnitude / 60; ...digits as today using magnitude % 60...`. CHAIN (returns int minutes): HOP1 DateFormatUtils.wallClockOffsetMinutes(Calendar) computes instant/wall as in LEX-01 -> HOP2 DateUtils.wallClockOffset(long instant, long wall) DEFINER `final long offset = instant - wall; return DurationFormatUtils.toMinutes(offset);` -> HOP3 DurationFormatUtils.toMinutes(long millis) `return (int) (millis / DateUtils.MILLIS_PER_MINUTE);`. GOLD add inside the nested class `private static char designatorSign(final int offsetMinutes)`: javadoc 'Sign of the designator for an offset in minutes.'; BUG LINE `return offsetMinutes < 0 ? '-' : '+';` CORRECT `return offsetMinutes > 0 ? '-' : '+';`. TRIGGER FastDatePrinterTest::testFormat; FAILURE TEXT: org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[-]0500> but was:<[+]0500>. Gold key for scoring: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule::designatorSign (catalog spells nested classes with `$`).
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter$TimeZoneNumberRule#designatorSign — same argument as LEX-01: the chain's output is UTC - local by hop 2's explicit parameter semantics, and this is the only method mis-applying it; the control's swapped literals are what moved here.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateUtils::wallClockOffset rank 1 (definer); or the facade appendTo (same nested class, different method) rank 1; a minority of runs may spell the right method with a dot-qualified class and be scored wrong.
ideas.model_specificity: The scorer-artifact component depends on each model's FQCN spelling habits (both observed to use `$`); the attribution component is model-agnostic. Ranked below LEX-01 because moving the gold next to the facade makes it more salient.

ideas.title: Mirror attack: strip the gold of every witness and transplant them (contract javadoc, original locals and constants) onto an executed, correct decoy hop (Lang Conversion)
ideas.mechanism: Tests the pure lexical hypothesis: the gold becomes `NumberUtils.place(long a, long b, int i, int k, int w, long m)` with no javadoc, single-letter locals and no distinctive constant, while BitField.widen carries the facade's original contract paragraph ('little endian, Lsb0', '@param at the position of the lsb, in bits'), the locals `shift`/`mask`/`bits`, the constants 32/0xffffffffL and the correct per-word mask formula. Prediction from the data: both models compute the arithmetic in the gold body anyway (the 21.6x host-file experiment and the same-depth decoys moved nothing), so this should barely dent Acc@1; included to bound the family's floor and as a component for the stronger attacks.
ideas.construction: Base: installed CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01 patch on Lang-1f. EDIT 1 src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/BitField.java widen(run, initial, at, width, field): javadoc becomes the original intArrayToLong paragraph ('Places a run of int values into a long using the default (little endian, Lsb0) byte and bit ordering ... @param at the position of the lsb, in bits, in the result'); body `final long[] words = new long[run.length]; final long[] masks = new long[run.length]; for (int i = 0; i < run.length; i++) { final int shift = i * 32 + at; final long bits = 0xffffffffL & run[i]; final long mask = 0xffffffffL << shift; words[i] = bits; masks[i] = mask; } return ObjectUtils.combine(words, masks, initial, at, width);` (correct masks, executed). EDIT 2 ObjectUtils.combine(long[] words, long[] masks, long initial, int at, int width): loop `total = NumberUtils.place(total, words[i], i, at, width, masks[i]);`. EDIT 3 GOLD rename NumberUtils.overlay -> `public static long place(final long a, final long b, final int i, final int k, final int w, final long m)` with NO javadoc; body BUG LINE `final int s = (i + k) * w; return (a & ~m) | (b << s);` CORRECT `final int s = i * w + k;`. TRIGGER ConversionTest::testLang1112: mask from the decoy is correct (bits 8..39 cleared) but the word is shifted by 256 -> 0. FAILURE TEXT: expected:<64729929216> but was:<252851286>.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils#place — the only hop whose shift disagrees with the (correct) mask it receives; the decoy's arithmetic is verifiably right for both assertions.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: Gold expected at rank 1 in most runs; when wrong, BitField::widen (carries the contract and the recognisable formula) or ObjectUtils::combine.
ideas.model_specificity: Model-agnostic; both models evaluate the gold's arithmetic regardless of naming. Possibly a little more effective on weaker tiers that lean on javadoc.

ideas.title: Wrong-twin parser: UTF-16 byte input is parsed by ReaderBasedJsonParser, gold is a name-identical twin of a UTF8StreamJsonParser method
ideas.mechanism: Claude greps one symbol per call and never scans; it chooses WHICH file to grep from a prior. The test builds the parser with the ubiquitous suite idiom createParserUsingStream(f, JSON, "UTF-16BE") and passes bytes, so the prior says UTF8StreamJsonParser. But ByteSourceJsonBootstrapper.constructParser only builds UTF8StreamJsonParser for detected UTF-8; UTF-16 bytes are wrapped by constructReader() and handled by ReaderBasedJsonParser. Both parsers declare _decodeEscaped() with byte-for-byte the same switch table, so the model that opens the UTF-8 twin sees nothing wrong, has no further lead, and (per the observed 0-1-calls-after-first-plausible-method behaviour) submits the twin at rank 1 with the Reader twin as a hedge at best. Neither model searched a gold name before entering a chain in 0/56 runs; here there is no chain to enter, only a class choice, and the class choice is made by encoding detection code the model never has a reason to read.

Leave UTF8StreamJsonParser._decodeEscaped (line ~2709, identical table) untouched. ideas.wrong_answer_expected: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.UTF8StreamJsonParser::_decodeEscaped at rank 1 (structurally identical twin); secondary: UTF8StreamJsonParser::_finishString2, ParserBase::getText / ReaderBasedJsonParser::getText, TextBuffer::contentsAsString
ideas.model_specificity: Strongest against Claude's file-targeted one-hop grep (it must pick a file before grepping). GPT-5.6's repository-wide greps for _decodeEscaped surface both twins side by side and the missing ++ is then visible, so GPT is expected to be ~0.7 Acc@1; the attack degrades if the model recalls that Jackson's bootstrapper hands non-UTF-8 bytes to a Reader.

ideas.title: Size-threshold dispatch: MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix silently returns BlockRealMatrix above 4096 elements; gold is BlockRealMatrix.getRow while the obvious class inherits AbstractRealMatrix.getRow
ideas.mechanism: Models resolve `RealMatrix m = MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix(data)` to the canonical implementation Array2DRowRealMatrix and grep getRow there. Array2DRowRealMatrix does not override getRow, so the search lands on AbstractRealMatrix.getRow (a 5-line loop over getEntry that is plainly correct), and the model drifts to Array2DRowRealMatrix.getEntry/copyIn or MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix. The real receiver is chosen by `data.length * data[0].length <= 4096` (MatrixUtils.java line 134), a rule that is invisible unless the factory body is read. The BlockRealMatrix.getRow bug is written to fire only when both block dimensions exceed one (rows and columns > 52), so every small-matrix test and every Array2DRow test passes, and a model that reads BlockRealMatrix sees a plausible-looking index expression it must compare against sibling methods to refute.

Edit src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/linear/BlockRealMatrix.java, public double[] getRow(final int row) (line ~1086): change `final double[] block = blocks[iBlock * blockColumns + jBlock];` to `final double[] block = blocks[jBlock * blockRows + iBlock];` (transposed block index; identical whenever blockRows==1 or blockColumns==1). Trigger test added to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math3/linear/MatrixUtilsTest.java: `@Test public void testCreateRealMatrixLargeGetRow() { final int n = 70; double[][] data = new double[n][n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) data[i][j] = 100.0 * i + j; RealMatrix m = MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix(data); Assert.assertArrayEquals(data[60], m.getRow(60), 0.0); }` (70*70=4900 > 4096 so BlockRealMatrix is chosen, blockRows=blockColumns=2; row 60 is in block row 1 so element 0 is already wrong and the failure index does not leak the value 52). Failure text: `arrays first differed at element [0]; expected:<6000.0> but was:<852.0>` (actual value taken from block (0,1): data[8][52]=852). Collateral: BlockRealMatrixTest's large multiply test (p=182,q=130 at line ~343-366) also fails; nothing else. Gold: org.apache.commons.math3.linear.BlockRealMatrix::getRow.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.math3.linear.BlockRealMatrix::getRow — sole edited line; BlockRealMatrix.getEntry, toBlocksLayout, getColumn and every other accessor still use iBlock*blockColumns+jBlock, so the only consistent fix is in getRow.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.math3.linear.AbstractRealMatrix::getRow or org.apache.commons.math3.linear.MatrixUtils::createRealMatrix at rank 1 when the dispatch is missed; org.apache.commons.math3.linear.BlockRealMatrix::toBlocksLayout when BlockRealMatrix is reached but the definer of the block layout is blamed
ideas.model_specificity: Hurts any model that skips reading the factory body; Claude's 6-call budget makes skipping likely. GPT-5.6's habit of grepping the type name repository-wide will surface the 4096 rule in MatrixUtils and the three getRow definitions together, giving it ~0.65.

ideas.title: Producer/consumer across the archive: ZipArchiveOutputStream records the local-header offset 4 bytes late; the failure surfaces as an exception inside ZipFile (the reader)
ideas.mechanism: The failing signal (stack trace) is entirely on the reader side: ZipFile.<init> -> resolveLocalFileHeaderData -> ZipArchiveEntry.setExtra -> ExtraFieldUtils.parse (ZipException 'data starting at 0 is in unknown format' wrapped in RuntimeException) or RuntimeException 'failed to skip file name in local file header'. Both models weight frames of the stack trace and the methods that DEFINE the wrong quantity (dataOffset computed in resolveLocalFileHeaderData; headerOffset read in populateFromCentralDirectory). The gold is on the writer side and is only reachable through a data structure (the `offsets` HashMap) whose put and get live in different methods (writeLocalFileHeader / writeCentralFileHeader), then through the archive bytes themselves. Even a model that reaches the writer sees writeCentralFileHeader emit `offsets.get(ze)` (the definer of the central-directory field) before it finds the put.
ideas.construction: Project Compress-1f at /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v2/screening/Compress. Edit src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/ZipArchiveOutputStream.java, protected void writeLocalFileHeader(ZipArchiveEntry ze) (line ~660): change `offsets.put(ze, ZipLong.getBytes(written));` to `offsets.put(ze, ZipLong.getBytes(written + WORD));` (records the offset of the byte after the LFH signature instead of the signature itself; ZipArchiveInputStream never reads central-directory offsets so streaming round trips still pass). Trigger test added to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/ZipTestCase.java (extends AbstractTestCase, has temp dir `dir`): `public void testZipFileReadsEntriesWrittenByArchiveOutputStream() throws Exception { File out = new File(dir, "roundtrip.zip"); ZipArchiveOutputStream zos = new ZipArchiveOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(out)); ZipArchiveEntry e = new ZipArchiveEntry("ab/hello.txt"); byte[] body = "hello, zip".getBytes("US-ASCII"); zos.putArchiveEntry(e); zos.write(body); zos.closeArchiveEntry(); zos.close(); ZipFile zf = new ZipFile(out); try { ZipArchiveEntry read = zf.getEntry("ab/hello.txt"); assertNotNull(read); assertTrue(Arrays.equals(body, IOUtils.toByteArray(zf.getInputStream(read)))); } finally { ZipFile.closeQuietly(zf); } }`. With the +4 offset, resolveLocalFileHeaderData reads the file-name length from the first two name bytes ('ab' = 0x6261 = 25185) and skipBytes hits EOF, so the failure text is `java.lang.RuntimeException: failed to skip file name in local file header at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.resolveLocalFileHeaderData(ZipFile.java:520) at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.<init>(ZipFile.java:190) ...` (build once to pin the exact shape; a short name can instead surface as ZipException from ExtraFieldUtils.parse). Collateral: UTF8ZipFilesTest cases that read ZipArchiveOutputStream output with ZipFile also fail. Gold: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveOutputStream::writeLocalFileHeader.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveOutputStream::writeLocalFileHeader — the only edited line; the ZIP spec defines the central-directory field as the offset of the LFH signature, ZipFile implements the spec correctly, and writeCentralFileHeader merely copies the stored bytes.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile::resolveLocalFileHeaderData at rank 1 (throwing frame and definer of dataOffset); alternatives ZipFile::populateFromCentralDirectory, ExtraFieldUtils::parse, ZipArchiveOutputStream::writeCentralFileHeader
ideas.model_specificity: Model-agnostic in mechanism (stack-trace anchoring is shared), but Claude's refusal to run the test or inspect the produced archive (e.g. with `unzip -l`/hexdump) removes its only cheap way to see that the central directory is what is wrong; GPT-5.6's verification calls may do exactly that and recover.

ideas.title: Cached maximum explode percent in PiePlot: writer (setExplodePercent) breaks the cache, consumer (drawPie/getMaximumExplodePercent) defines the wrong value, dataset callback also touches it
ideas.mechanism: Generalises the only known double failure (CHART-PIE-03): models attribute to the method that DEFINES the wrong-looking quantity. Here the test observes a section entity's bounds after drawing; the pie area is defined in drawPie from `percent = mep / (1 + mep)` with mep = getMaximumExplodePercent(), which returns a cached field. The cache is invalidated correctly in a new PiePlot.datasetChanged override (reached only through dataset.addChangeListener registration in setDataset) and incorrectly maintained in setExplodePercent (monotone update). The model must (a) leave drawPie, the definer of the wrong area, (b) leave getMaximumExplodePercent, the definer of the wrong mep, (c) grep the field to find two writers and decide which of the incremental update or the callback invalidation is the fault. The relation between the consumer and the gold is a field, not a call, so 'grep the next symbol' stops at getMaximumExplodePercent.
ideas.construction: Project Chart-1f at /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v2/screening/Chart (src dir `source`, tests `tests`). Edit source/org/jfree/chart/plot/PiePlot.java: (1) add field `private transient double maximumExplodePercent = -1.0;` next to explodePercentages (line ~386); (2) rewrite public double getMaximumExplodePercent() (line 1648) to `if (this.maximumExplodePercent < 0.0) { double result = 0.0; if (this.dataset != null) { iterate keys as today, result = Math.max(...) } this.maximumExplodePercent = result; } return this.maximumExplodePercent;`; (3) add `public void datasetChanged(DatasetChangeEvent event) { this.maximumExplodePercent = -1.0; super.datasetChanged(event); }` (PiePlot registers itself via dataset.addChangeListener(this) in setDataset line 662, so key additions/removals invalidate through the callback); (4) in setExplodePercent (line 1632) the intended line is `this.maximumExplodePercent = -1.0;` before fireChangeEvent(); the injected one-line bug replaces it with `this.maximumExplodePercent = Math.max(this.maximumExplodePercent, percent);` (fast path that is wrong when the largest percentage is lowered). Also reset the cache in the clone()/readObject paths if present (keep testCloning/testSerialization green). Trigger test added to tests/org/jfree/chart/plot/junit/PiePlotTests.java: `public void testExplodeMarginShrinksWhenPercentLowered() { DefaultPieDataset ds = new DefaultPieDataset(); ds.setValue("A", 1.0); ds.setValue("B", 3.0); PiePlot plot = new PiePlot(ds); plot.setExplodePercent("A", 0.5); plot.setExplodePercent("A", 0.0); plot.setExplodePercent("B", 0.0); BufferedImage img = new BufferedImage(400, 300, BufferedImage.TYPE_INT_RGB); Graphics2D g2 = img.createGraphics(); ChartRenderingInfo info = new ChartRenderingInfo(); plot.draw(g2, new Rectangle2D.Double(0, 0, 400, 300), null, null, info.getPlotInfo()); g2.dispose(); PieSectionEntity a = (PieSectionEntity) info.getEntityCollection().getEntity(0); assertEquals(<width recorded from a correct build>, a.getArea().getBounds2D().getWidth(), 1.0E-6); }` (with all percentages back at 0 the pie must fill the explode area; with the stale cache 0.5 the pie is shrunk by 0.5/1.5). Failure text: `expected:<W_full> but was:<W_shrunk>` (record both numerically from a control build). Gold: org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot::setExplodePercent.
ideas.gold: org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot::setExplodePercent — the cache contract (invalidate on every write to explodePercentages) is owned by the writer; getMaximumExplodePercent and drawPie behave correctly for a valid cache, and datasetChanged already invalidates correctly for key-set changes.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot::getMaximumExplodePercent at rank 1 (definer of the stale value, contains the cache read), or org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot::drawPie (definer of the pie area); org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot::getArcBounds by analogy with the known Chart pattern
ideas.model_specificity: Targets the shared definer bias measured in CHART-PIE-03 (GPT 5/5, Claude 3/3 ranked the definer first). Less model-specific than SSN-01; both models find setExplodePercent eventually, so the attack works only through rank order.

ideas.title: Aggregate translator consumed-count bug: twelve `translate` methods, a lightning-rod loop in the base class, and a gold selected at run time by input content
ideas.mechanism: StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 runs UNESCAPE_HTML4 = AggregateTranslator(LookupTranslator x3, NumericEntityUnescaper). Which translator handles a position is decided at run time by the input (first non-zero return wins), so 'grep the next symbol' from unescapeHtml4 yields a field initialiser, then a method name that resolves to 12 declarations across 10 classes. The base loop CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer) advances with `pos += Character.charCount(Character.codePointAt(input, pt))` (pt, not pos+pt), which reads as an obvious bug and is on the path for every character; it is the natural rank-1 for a model that sees the output contain one leftover character. The gold is the return-value arithmetic of NumericEntityUnescaper.translate, five lines from the end of a 60-line method, correct for decimal entities and wrong only for hex ones.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f at /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v1/screening/lang (20 s suite). Edit src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/translate/NumericEntityUnescaper.java, public int translate(CharSequence input, int index, Writer out) (return at line ~136): change `return 2 + end - start + (isHex ? 1 : 0) + (semiNext ? 1 : 0);` to `return 2 + end - start + (semiNext ? 1 : 0);` (the 'x' of a hex entity is written but not counted as consumed, so the driving loop re-emits the character after the entity). Trigger test added to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/StringEscapeUtilsTest.java: `public void testUnescapeHtml4HexEntityFollowedByText() { assertEquals("Ab", StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4("Ab")); assertEquals("A b", StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4("A b")); }`. Failure text: `junit.framework.ComparisonFailure: expected:<A[]b> but was:<A[;]b>`. Collateral: existing testUnescapeHexCharsHtml4 (€Ÿ) and the &#x surrogate loop in testUnescapeHtml4, plus NumericEntityUnescaperTest hex cases, also fail deterministically. Gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper::translate.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper::translate — the CharSequenceTranslator contract is that translate returns the number of code points consumed; the hex prefix was consumed and must be counted; AggregateTranslator and the base loop honour the contract and cannot know an 'x' was eaten.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.CharSequenceTranslator::translate at rank 1 (the odd-looking pos-advance loop), or org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.AggregateTranslator::translate; LookupTranslator::translate as a same-name distractor
ideas.model_specificity: The lexical cue '&#x' points at the only class whose source mentions hex, which helps both models discover the gold; the attack lives in rank order (lightning-rod loop vs. subtle return arithmetic) and should affect Claude and GPT similarly. Weak Claude, which reads less of the 60-line method, is hit harder.

ideas.title: Strategy list built from a format pattern: FastDatePrinter.selectNumberRule hands the padded rule the wrong width; the inner Rule class that emits the digits is the visible definer
ideas.mechanism: FastDateFormat.getInstance(pattern).format(date) -> FastDatePrinter.parsePattern (100-line switch over pattern letters) -> selectNumberRule(field, tokenLen) -> one of 12 private static inner Rule classes -> applyRules loops rule.appendTo(buf, calendar). The output digits are produced by PaddedNumberField.appendTo (the definer of the padding), which is correct for its constructor argument; the gold is the dispatcher that constructed it with padding-1. The path crosses a heterogeneous list of function objects (List<Rule>), and the same method name appendTo exists 12 times in one file, so a grep for appendTo returns a wall of inner classes; the model must instead reason backwards through a constructor argument. Inner-class candidates are also awkward to name in FQCN::method form, pushing predictions toward whichever top-level method 'looks' involved (format, applyRules, parsePattern).
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f at /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v1/screening/lang. Edit src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinter.java, protected NumberRule selectNumberRule(final int field, final int padding) (line 356): change `default: return new PaddedNumberField(field, padding);` to `default: return new PaddedNumberField(field, padding - 1);` (3+ letter numeric tokens such as SSS/yyyy/DDD/FFF get one digit less minimum width; values that already have enough digits are unaffected, so most existing formats still pass). Trigger test added to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateFormatTest.java: `public void testMillisecondPadding() { Calendar cal = Calendar.getInstance(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")); cal.clear(); cal.set(2013, Calendar.MARCH, 4, 5, 6, 7); cal.set(Calendar.MILLISECOND, 5); FastDateFormat f = FastDateFormat.getInstance("HH:mm:ss.SSS", TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")); assertEquals("05:06:07.005", f.format(cal)); }`. Failure text: `expected:<05:06:07.0[0]5> but was:<05:06:07.0[]5>`. Collateral: existing tests formatting SSS with ms < 100 or DDD/yyyy with short values (check FastDateFormatTest/DateFormatUtilsTest; expect 1-3). Gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter::selectNumberRule. Scoring note: decoys are inner classes (FastDatePrinter$PaddedNumberField::appendTo); make sure the scorer treats such predictions as non-gold regardless of $ vs . spelling.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter::selectNumberRule — the only edited line; PaddedNumberField pads exactly to the width it was constructed with, and parsePattern passes the correct token length, so the width loss happens solely in the dispatcher.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter$PaddedNumberField::appendTo (definer of the digit string) or, because inner classes are awkward to name, org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter::parsePattern / ::applyRules / org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat::format
ideas.model_specificity: Claude's grep -A30 on 'selectNumberRule' shows the whole switch, so once it reaches the dispatcher the bug is visible; the attack relies on it stopping earlier at PaddedNumberField or parsePattern. GPT-5.6 reads more and is expected ~0.7.

ideas.title: Header-id registry: ExtraFieldUtils instantiates the parser class from a static map keyed by two bytes of the fixture; round-trip test makes the encoder the visible definer
ideas.mechanism: ZipArchiveEntry.setCentralDirectoryExtra(bytes) -> ExtraFieldUtils.parse(bytes,false) -> createExtraField(headerId) -> implementations.get(headerId) (HashMap<ZipShort,Class>, filled by register(...) in a static block) -> Class.newInstance() -> ze.parseFromCentralDirectoryData -> AsiExtraField.parseFromLocalFileData. ideas.title: Field-mediated flow in TextBuffer: finishCurrentSegment mis-accumulates _segmentSize, size() defines the wrong length, and the parser's _finishString2 offers a competing fix location
ideas.mechanism: getTextLength() -> TextBuffer.size() -> `_segmentSize + _currentSize`. The wrong number is DEFINED in size(); its inputs are fields written in five methods (resetWith*, finishCurrentSegment, expand, setCurrentLength). The parser calls finishCurrentSegment() when a segment fills without first calling setCurrentLength(outPtr), so the injected `_segmentSize += _currentSize` counts zero for every finished segment. A model that finds it must still decide between two defensible fixes: TextBuffer.finishCurrentSegment (use the segment's full length, as expand() does) or ReaderBasedJsonParser/UTF8StreamJsonParser._finishString2 (set the current length before finishing). Behavioural ownership is ambiguous, which the prior data says models handle, but here the competing owner is in a different class and (if combined with SSN-01) the wrong twin. getText() stays correct (StringBuilder path), which removes the contents as evidence and focuses attention on size().
ideas.construction: Project JacksonCore-1f at /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v2/screening/JacksonCore. Edit src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/util/TextBuffer.java, public char[] finishCurrentSegment() (line ~582): change `_segmentSize += oldLen;` to `_segmentSize += _currentSize;`. Verify emptyAndGetCurrentSegment() zeroes _currentSize (line ~544) so finished segments contribute 0. Trigger test added to src/test/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/json/TestJsonParser.java: `public void testLongStringTextLength() throws Exception { StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(1200); for (int i = 0; i < 1200; ++i) sb.append((char) ('a' + (i % 26))); String value = sb.toString(); JsonParser jp = createParserUsingReader("[\"" + value + "\"]"); assertToken(JsonToken.START_ARRAY, jp.nextToken()); assertToken(JsonToken.VALUE_STRING, jp.nextToken()); assertEquals(value, jp.getText()); assertEquals(1200, jp.getTextLength()); jp.close(); }` (TEXT_BUFFER starts at 200 chars and grows 200,300,450 so three segments are finished; the final tail is 250). Failure text: `junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: expected:<1200> but was:<250>`. Collateral: any existing test calling getTextCharacters()/getTextLength() on strings longer than 200 chars (buildResultArray then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException). Gold: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.util.TextBuffer::finishCurrentSegment.
ideas.gold: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.util.TextBuffer::finishCurrentSegment — the TextBuffer contract (see expand(), which adds curr.length) is that a finished segment counts in full; the parsers' usage (finishCurrentSegment when outPtr reaches outBuf.length) is the documented pattern, so the accumulation line is the fault.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.ReaderBasedJsonParser::_finishString2 (or UTF8StreamJsonParser::_finishString2 if combined with SSN-01) at rank 1 as the 'should have called setCurrentLength' owner; com.fasterxml.jackson.core.util.TextBuffer::size or ::setCurrentLength as definer candidates
ideas.model_specificity: Both models grep the field and see the adjacent expand() using curr.length, so discovery is near-certain; the miss comes from ownership judgement, which the earlier chain experiments show models usually resolve toward the deepest visible arithmetic. ideas.title: Pinned inward drift: CHART-PIE-03 regenerated on fresh hosts with an independently pinned definer

Neither model ever greps hop names in tests before submitting (0/56), and neither runs the suite, so pinning the definer with a second caller and a unit test makes the gold the unique suite-green fix without changing anything the model looks at. Fresh hosts/names avoid any memorisation of the earlier CompassPlot/StandardDialScale/PlotUtilities/Plot/ShapeUtilities chain.

ideas.title: Inverted borrow sense in Fraction.getFraction(whole, numerator, denominator) - the PIE-03 sign trap on Lang integers
ideas.mechanism: Same mechanism as OWN-01 but in a 20-second suite and with integer arithmetic the model can and will simulate: the real method combines `whole*den + num` for whole >= 0 and `whole*den - num` for whole < 0. The chain expresses that as a 'borrow' sign defined in one hop and applied in another. The definer returns `whole < 0 ? 1 : -1`, which reads as inverted to every reader ('the sign should follow the whole'), while the gold applies it with `scaled + borrow * numerator`, which reads as the natural 'combine'. Reversing the definer or flipping the gold's operator are trigger-equivalent on every assertion of the existing test (0/2: 0+(-1)*1 = -1 vs 1; -1 6/10: -10+6 = -4 vs -16), so simulation cannot separate them and the definer heuristic picks the definer. Pinning the definer with a direct unit test on `borrow` makes the gold the unique suite-green single-method fix.

ideas.title: Memory inversion on Percentile: a zero-based position definer versus a gold that reproduces the memorised `intPos - 1` indexing
ideas.mechanism: Exploits the fact that both models have memorised Commons Math's Percentile.evaluate (`pos = p * (n + 1) / 100`, `lower = sorted[intPos - 1]`, `upper = sorted[intPos]`). The correct chain adopts a different but valid convention: the definer returns a ZERO-based fractional position (`p*(n+1)/100 - 1`), and the correct consumer indexes `sorted[intPos]`, `sorted[intPos + 1]`. The injected bug makes the consumer index `intPos - 1`/`intPos`, i.e. the gold's body is exactly the line the model remembers as correct, while the definer's `- 1` is the line that deviates from memory. Removing the definer's `- 1` and fixing the gold's indices are trigger-equivalent on the trigger inputs, so simulation cannot discriminate and the model resolves by memory plus the definer heuristic: it blames the definer. The definer is pinned by the existing PercentileTest#testPercentile p=75 case through the zero-based edge guard in the consumer (a definer-only fix returns 4.0 instead of 3.75) and by a new StatUtilsTest assertion.

ideas.title: Skewness finite-sample factor: population moments in the definer, the memorised n/((n-1)(n-2)) factor in the gold
ideas.mechanism: Memory inversion where mental simulation is impossible (22-element testArray, floating point), so the model must reason symbolically and does so from its memory of Commons Math's Skewness.evaluate: variance divided by (length - 1), then `skew = n/((n-1)(n-2)) * accum3`. The chain computes POPULATION central moments (m2, m3 both divided by n) in one definer, standardises g1 = m3/m2^1.5, and the gold applies the finite-sample correction. The correct factor for population moments is sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2); the injected bug uses the memorised n/((n-1)(n-2)). The model sees `/ n` in the definer ('should be n - 1, that is what Commons Math does') and the familiar factor in the gold ('canonical G1 formula') and blames the definer or the standardisation hop. Unlike OWN-01/02 the two candidate fixes are NOT trigger-equivalent (a definer-only fix gives 1.4374/21 ~ 0.068, not 1.4374), so the gold is pinned by the trigger itself; but no model verifies fixes numerically.

ideas.title: DOS date month: the producer omits the 1-based normalisation, the packer that already normalises the year takes the blame
ideas.mechanism: Direction 2 of the family (gold = producer). ZipUtil.toDosTime packs Calendar fields into the DOS date/time word; DOS months are 1-12, java.util.Calendar months 0-11, so a +1 must live somewhere. The chain extracts raw fields in the producer (gold, whose javadoc promises month 1-12 but whose body returns cal.get(Calendar.MONTH)) and packs them in a layout method that visibly normalises the year (`(year - 1980) << 9`) but leaves the month untouched (`month << 5`). The model, decoding the 1<<21 difference in the failure, knows a +1 is missing and places it where normalisation already happens and where the bit layout is DEFINED: the packer. The packer is right under its own contract and is pinned by the inverse decoder and by every reader of the field; the producer violates its javadoc. Weaker than direction 1 because the missing correction can be attributed to either site and memory of the real `time.getMonth() + 1` line helps the model, but it is a genuinely realistic bug class.

ideas.title: Token column: the shared helper drops the 'pointer is past the character' -1, and the real 0-to-1-based +1 in ParserBase.getTokenColumnNr takes the blame
ideas.mechanism: Direction 2 with a compensating pair that is REAL: ReaderBasedJsonParser/UTF8StreamJsonParser set `_tokenInputCol = _inputPtr - _currInputRowStart - 1` (the pointer has already advanced past the token's first char) and ParserBase#getTokenColumnNr returns `col + 1` with the comment 'convert from 0-based to 1-based'. Deduplicating the three identical assignment sites into one helper whose body is `inputPtr - rowStart` (documented as 0-based) yields column 2 for a token at column 1. Two trigger-equivalent one-line fixes exist: restore the `- 1` in the helper or delete the `+ 1` in getTokenColumnNr. The helper's body reads naturally ('column = pointer minus row start') unless the reader knows the pointer semantics, which requires reading _skipWSOrEnd; the `+ 1` is a visible, wrong-looking correction on the data path. Claude, reading one grep hit per call, tends to stop at the visible correction; GPT is more likely to chase _inputPtr. The +1 is pinned by getCurrentLocation's identical `+ 1 // 1-based` and by the -1 sentinel handling around it.

ideas.title: Facade role swap in Conversion.intToHex: srcPos and dstPos exchanged into a neutrally named, fully coherent chain
ideas.mechanism: Facade-as-gold variant: every low-level method is correct and self-consistent; the facade passes the bit position where the chain expects the character index and vice versa. The failing test (existing testIntToHex) shows hex digits appearing at index 0 instead of index 3 and taken from the wrong bit offset, so the model quickly infers 'positions confused'. The attack relies on (i) Claude's `grep -n 'intToHex' -A30` never showing the facade javadoc that defines which parameter is the bit position, (ii) the chain's parameter names being neutral (`from`, `at`) so the swapped call reads as plausible, and (iii) the depth prior pushing the model to blame the hop that computes `shift = i * 4 + from` (the definer of the digit) rather than the one-line facade. It is the weakest idea here because the facade line lists both positions in swapped order right under a signature that names them, which a careful reader will spot.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f, checkout /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/core-benchmark-scaleup-v1/screening/lang. H3 org.apache.commons.lang3.CharSequenceUtils#place(final String into, final int at, final char[] digits): the real append-or-setCharAt idiom lifted from intToHex (`if (at + i == sb.length()) sb.append(c) else sb.setCharAt(at + i, c)`). ideas.title: Pre-positioned mask contract: unpositioned mask built at hop 2, asymmetry visible only at hop 5, contract only in a second real consumer (Lang Conversion.intArrayToLong)
ideas.mechanism: Both models attribute to the stage whose code looks locally inconsistent, not to the deepest stage (PIE-03: all 8 runs blamed the hop that defined the sign). Here the gold line in EnumUtils.compose, `final long mask = (1L << width) - 1;`, is the verbatim line of the already-validated CONVERSION-LONG template (where it was correct), so it reads as innocent on the single pass Claude makes (grep hop, -A30, next hop). Hop 5 NumberUtils.overlay shifts the mask by `index*width` but the word by `at + index*width`: an asymmetry that reads as 'forgot `at` in the mask shift' and matches the failure text exactly (actual = expected truncated to the low 32 bits: 0x12345600 vs 0xF12345600). The only evidence that the mask is pre-positioned (BitField's real `_mask`/`_shift_count` idiom) is in BitField.java, whose `setValue` is rewired onto overlay with its positioned `_mask`; that file is never on the chain. Claude searched a gold's callers in 0/56 runs and submits <=1 call after the last hop, so it never sees it; GPT-5.6 reaches it only via a repo-wide usage grep of `overlay(`, and its habitual hypothesis check (does the overlay fix make the trigger pass?) says yes, because only BitFieldTest would break and it never runs that. Depth prior reinforces the wrong pick.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f. Base: install /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/diagnostic-noncanonical-v3/new_bug_variants/Lang/bug-1/L20/CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01/variant.patch + its test.patch (adds ConversionTest.testLang1112), then edit four methods. (1) EnumUtils.compose(int[] run, long initial, int at): body `final int width = Integer.SIZE; final long mask = (1L << width) - 1; return BitField.widen(run, initial, at, width, mask);` -- this unchanged-looking line IS the bug; correct is `((1L << width) - 1) << at`. Javadoc: 'Composes a run of int values into a long, deriving the value width and the mask of the first value.' (2) BitField.widen(int[] run, long initial, int at, int width, long mask): `words[i] = 0xffffffffL & run[i];` (the original facade's own idiom; `mask` is forwarded, not used) then `return ObjectUtils.combine(words, initial, at, width, mask);`. (3) ObjectUtils.combine unchanged (`total = NumberUtils.overlay(total, words[i], i, at, width, mask)`). (4) NumberUtils.overlay(long holder, long word, int index, int at, int width, long mask): `final long m = mask << (index * width); final int shift = at + index * width; return (holder & ~m) | ((word << shift) & m);` Javadoc deliberately non-pointed: '@param mask the mask selecting the first value of the run', '@param at the position of the lsb of the first value' (do NOT write 'positioned'). (5) Second real consumer: BitField.setValue(int holder, int value) becomes `return (int) NumberUtils.overlay(holder, value, 0, _shift_count, Integer.bitCount(_mask), _mask);` (add import org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils; setShortValue already delegates). Failure text: `junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: expected:<64729929216> but was:<305419776>` (a 32-bit truncation signature). Gold file src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/EnumUtils.java. ideas.model_specificity: Claude Opus 5.5: near-certain miss (one grep per hop, never searches callers, submits right after the last hop; the -A grep also hides overlay's javadoc). GPT-5.6: misses unless its repo-wide `overlay(` grep lands on BitField.setValue and it reasons from `_mask` being positioned (it did search helper usages in the HA block, so ~30% recovery); its mental verification of the overlay fix passes the trigger and reinforces the wrong hop. ideas.title: Pre-positioned words: hop 3 shifts each word by `at`, hop 5 gold re-adds `at` in the textbook placement formula (Lang Conversion.intArrayToLong)
ideas.mechanism: Mirror image of CTX-01, designed to separate the definer heuristic from the depth prior. The gold's line `(holder & ~m) | (word << (at + index*width))` is the canonical placement formula and is internally consistent with the mask line directly above it (`m = field << (at + index*width)`), so it reads as correct; the odd-looking step is hop 3 `widen` computing `(0xffffffffL & run[i]) << at`. The failure text says the value landed at bit 16 instead of 8 (shift applied twice), so the model must decide which of the two `<< at` is redundant. PIE-03 behaviour predicts the stage that introduced the pre-shift (widen, the definer) is blamed and the symmetric formula kept. The contract lives only in widen's javadoc ('to the given field at the given position'), which sits above the declaration and outside Claude's `-A30` grep window in most of its hop reads; GPT's `sed -n` ranges include it, which is why GPT is expected to do better here than in CTX-01.
ideas.construction: Project Lang-1f, same base patch as CTX-01 (CONVERSION-LONG-TREATMENT-01 variant + testLang1112). Edits: (1) BitField.widen(int[] run, long initial, int at, int width, long field): `words[i] = (0xffffffffL & run[i]) << at;` javadoc 'Widens the values of a run to the given field at the given position.' (2) EnumUtils.compose unchanged from the template (`field = (1L << width) - 1`, unpositioned). (3) ObjectUtils.combine unchanged (loop calling overlay(total, words[i], i, at, width, field)). (4) NumberUtils.overlay(long holder, long word, int index, int at, int width, long field): correct `final long m = field << (at + index * width); return (holder & ~m) | (word << (index * width));` ONE-LINE BUG: `| (word << (at + index * width))`. Javadoc '@param word the widened value' (neutral; the positioning contract is stated at widen). No second consumer is possible here (any correct caller of the buggy overlay would fail). Emulated: testLang1112 assertion 1 -> `expected:<64729929216> but was:<16570861879296>` (0xF12345600 vs 0xF1234560000); all existing dstPos=0 cases pass (at=0 makes the double shift a no-op, which is also why the fault survives testIntArrayToLong). Gold file src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.java.
ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils#overlay -- widen's documented job is to widen values to their field at the given position; combine and overlay therefore receive positioned words and overlay must shift by the index stride only. The alternative fix (drop widen's shift) contradicts widen's documented contract.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.lang3.BitField#widen at rank 1 (the visible pre-shift), overlay at rank 2-3.
ideas.model_specificity: Diagnostic pair with CTX-01: the gold is the deepest hop, so a wrong pick here is anti-depth and pro-definer. Claude (no javadoc in view) is predicted to blame widen; GPT-5.6, which reads the javadoc above the declaration, recovers about half the time.

ideas.title: Screen-angle negation as definer decoy: the Java2D y-down flip legitimately at hop 1, wrongly repeated at hop 5 (Chart SpiderWebPlot.getWebPoint)
ideas.mechanism: A sign fault that commutes through the chain, PIE-03 style. The real getWebPoint flips y with `-Math.sin`; in the chain the flip is moved to hop 1 as `screenAngle = -angle` (documented as the Java2D orientation change), and the gold at hop 5 subtracts the y offset (`centre.getY() - oy`), which is the textbook y-down idiom every model has seen, so the gold reads as correct and hop 1's negation reads as the spurious sign. Both one-line fixes pass the trigger. The evidence that the placement stage must be additive lives in other plots the models never open: PolarPlot.translateValueThetaRadiusToJava2D adds both components (`midY + yv * ...`) and SpiderWebPlot.draw's own angle bookkeeping uses `startAngle + direction.getFactor() * ...`. A passing x assertion and a passing angle-0 assertion are negative evidence that only the y flip is doubled.
ideas.construction: Project Chart-1f (source/, tests/). Facade SpiderWebPlot.getWebPoint(Rectangle2D bounds, double angle, double length) body -> `return Rotation.webPoint(bounds, angle, length);`. H1 org.jfree.chart.util.Rotation.webPoint(Rectangle2D bounds, double angle, double length): `double screenAngle = -angle; return ThermometerPlot.ray(bounds, screenAngle, length);` javadoc: 'Java2D's y-axis points down, so a data angle measured anticlockwise is a clockwise screen angle; the angle is negated before the point is resolved.' H2 org.jfree.chart.plot.ThermometerPlot.ray(Rectangle2D bounds, double screenAngle, double length): `double r = Math.toRadians(screenAngle); return WaferMapPlot.extend(bounds, Math.cos(r), Math.sin(r), length);` H3 org.jfree.chart.plot.WaferMapPlot.extend(Rectangle2D bounds, double ux, double uy, double length): `double ox = ux * length * bounds.getWidth() / 2; double oy = uy * length * bounds.getHeight() / 2; return RectangleAnchor.fromCentre(bounds, ox, oy);` H4 org.jfree.chart.util.RectangleAnchor.fromCentre(Rectangle2D bounds, double ox, double oy): `Point2D centre = new Point2D.Double(bounds.getCenterX(), bounds.getCenterY()); return LineUtilities.displace(centre, ox, oy);` H5 gold org.jfree.chart.util.LineUtilities.displace(Point2D centre, double ox, double oy): correct `return new Point2D.Double(centre.getX() + ox, centre.getY() + oy);` ONE-LINE BUG `centre.getY() - oy`. ideas.gold: org.jfree.chart.util.LineUtilities#displace -- hop 1's javadoc fixes the orientation change at the angle stage, so the placement stage must be additive; PolarPlot's original placement is additive; the second flip is the deviation from both.

GPT-5.6 reads the javadoc and about half the time concludes the second flip is the fault; removing the explanatory javadoc from hop 1 would push both models to hop 1 but makes ownership arbitrary.

ideas.title: Real inverted flag as the first plausible explanation: CpioUtil.byteArray2long's `if (!swapHalfWord)` prelude kept verbatim, byte-order fault moved into the halfword reader (Compress)
ideas.mechanism: The facade's real, untouched prelude has a genuine doc/code mismatch in Compress-1f: the javadoc says 'Halfwords can be swaped with setting swapHalfWord=true' while the code swaps when it is false. An LLM flags this on its first read (Claude run-001 in PIE-03 attributed on exactly this kind of doc/code disagreement). The injected fault (each halfword composed little-endian) is behaviourally indistinguishable from 'the facade swapped when it should not have' on every even-length input (swap-pairs then big-endian == little-endian halfwords), so the decoy explanation reproduces the observed value exactly and no arithmetic refutes it. Only the trigger's expectations, written against the real behaviour (false -> swapped pairs), show that the facade agrees with the test and the deep reader does not. The gold's formula is the same little-endian idiom as the real ZipShort.getValue two methods above it in the same class, so it reads as house style. Definer heuristic (the facade defines the byte order) and doc/code heuristic both point at the facade.
ideas.construction: Project Compress-1f. Facade org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioUtil.byteArray2long(byte[] number, boolean swapHalfWord): keep the copy, the odd-length check and the `if (!swapHalfWord) { pairwise swap }` loop verbatim; replace the `ret` accumulation loop with `return ZipUtil.wordValue(tmp_number);`. H1 org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipUtil.wordValue(byte[] bytes): `final int halfwords = bytes.length / 2; return ZipLong.fromHalfwords(bytes, halfwords);` javadoc 'Interprets an even number of bytes as 16-bit halfwords, most significant halfword first.' H2 org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipLong.fromHalfwords(byte[] bytes, int count): `long value = 0; for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) { value = (value << 16) | ZipShort.halfwordAt(bytes, 2 * i); } return value;` H3 gold org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipShort.halfwordAt(byte[] bytes, int offset): ONE-LINE BUG `return (TarBuffer.unsigned(bytes[offset + 1]) << 8) | TarBuffer.unsigned(bytes[offset]);` correct `(TarBuffer.unsigned(bytes[offset]) << 8) | TarBuffer.unsigned(bytes[offset + 1])`; javadoc 'Returns the halfword starting at the given offset.' H4 org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarBuffer.unsigned(byte b): `return b & 0xFF;`. Trigger: new test class src/test/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/cpio/CpioUtilTest.java (same package; CpioUtil is package-private) with testCompress104: `byte[] n = {1, 2, 3, 4}; assertEquals(0x02010403L, CpioUtil.byteArray2long(n, false)); assertEquals(0x01020304L, CpioUtil.byteArray2long(n, true)); assertEquals(0x0201L, CpioUtil.byteArray2long(new byte[] {1, 2}, false));` (expected values are the real method's outputs, emulated). Failure text: `junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: expected:<33620995> but was:<16909060>`. Collateral: the suite never reads old-binary cpio (bla.cpio magic is '070702'); the two magic probes in CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextCPIOEntry on the two ASCII bytes '07' evaluate to 0x3037/0x3730 under both versions, never 070707, so ASCII detection is unchanged; long2byteArray is untouched. ideas.gold: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipShort#halfwordAt -- the facade is the unchanged original whose behaviour the trigger encodes; the halfword reader is the only edited stage; the original accumulation `ret <<= 8; ret |= b` is big-endian within the halfword.
ideas.wrong_answer_expected: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioUtil#byteArray2long (the facade, for its `!swapHalfWord` prelude) at rank 1; ZipUtil#wordValue at rank 2; halfwordAt at rank 3-4.
